outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (shoulder dystocia, large for gestational age, neonatal intensive care unit admission, neonatal hypoglycemia, or respiratory distress syndrome)
cohort: 233 women with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and singleton pregnancy
finding: Among pregnant women with T2DM managed with either basal or NPH insulin regimen, the rates of composite neonatal morbidity and maternal complications were similar.
mod_finding: The study found that women with type 2 diabetes mellitus who received basal insulin analogs had a lower rate of primary cesarean delivery compared to those who received NPH insulin.
